description: Mutated HTTP/2 frame attack against an externally-launched H2C (HTTP/2 cleartext) target. Seed: a single HEADERS frame plus DATA frame for GET /plaintext, mutated by radamsa into invalid frame headers, malformed HPACK blocks, and oversized payloads. Each variant is fired over a fresh TCP connection that starts with the H2C connection preface. PRIMARY CHECK: after attack window + cooldown, target serves clean GET /health with HTTP/2 200 within 1s.
loopback_caveat: H2C cleartext only; H2-over-TLS not covered by this scenario. transport_mode=loopback-h2 mandatory.

attack_profile.rate_note: requests_per_second is a REQUESTED rate. Until 2026-08-26 the driver was single-threaded and every read timeout blocked it for the full socket deadline, so the first campaign requested 500 and achieved 3.4 (60 timeouts x 2.0 s consumed the whole 120 s window; radamsa generation was 1.1 % of it). The driver now fires from a worker pool and reports achieved_rps and backlog_skips -- a run that cannot reach this rate says so instead of letting this number stand in for what happened.
attack_profile.concurrency_note: Concurrency is part of the stimulus, not a harness detail: N connections at once is a different attack from N in sequence. It travels with the result and belongs in any comparison. Sizing: rps x incomplete-mutant fraction x socket timeout gives the worker-seconds per wall second the timeouts alone consume.

liveness_probe.note: Liveness probe uses curl --http2-prior-knowledge. nghttp may be used as fallback.

tolerance.rss_note: rss_growth_pct_max is measured against a baseline taken AFTER a warm-up (baseline_warmup_seconds in the artifact). Before 2026-08-26 the baseline was cold, so first-load JIT, metaspace fill and heap commit were charged to the attack: the first slowloris run read +34.9 % against this 5 % bound while its JFR put live heap after the forced GC at 9.5 MB. RSS remains a weak leak signal here -- see comparison_axis_note -- and a run without NMT leaves the non-heap remainder unattributed. Do not compare rss_bytes_delta across runs with different baseline_warmup_seconds. Both samples are additionally preceded by a forced GC (since 2026-08-27), so the delta compares two post-collection states -- retained memory. Before that date only the FINAL sample was, which compared a collected heap against an uncollected one and biased the delta toward understating growth; on destructive-radamsa-h2 it read -588 517 376 bytes. Artifacts from before that change are not comparable with later ones.
tolerance.hang_note: hang_count counts read timeouts on mutants the target was OBLIGED to answer: the buffer ends on a frame boundary AND a client-initiated stream was opened to END_HEADERS and half-closed by END_STREAM. Frame alignment alone is not enough and was the rule until 2026-08-26 -- an HTTP/1 idea in HTTP/2 clothing, since a lone well-formed SETTINGS frame is perfectly aligned and obliges the server to say nothing. Such a mutant timed out at the socket deadline and scored a hang against this max_hang_count: 0, so a correctly idle server would have failed the run; it fired once in 400 validation iterations. A truncated final frame leaves the target correctly waiting: incomplete-wait, not a hang.

response_note: response_count counts ONLY frames sent in answer to a mutant. It must not be read as "the target accepted the input" without that qualification, because RFC 9113 s3.4 makes the server's SETTINGS frame the mandatory first thing it sends after the preface -- which this driver sends intact by design -- so bytes always come back. The first campaign (20260826-192933) classified on the first bytes received and scored 60000/60000 as responses; measured against kernel 0.11.0, an intact preface followed by pure garbage, by a single zero byte, and by nothing at all all returned the identical 9-byte empty SETTINGS frame. That run's response_count is not comparable with any later one. The classifier now skips the frames a server sends unprompted (SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE) and decides on the next one.
outcome_details_note: findings.outcome_details histograms the target's GOAWAY and RST_STREAM error codes. On a campaign with zero crashes and zero hangs it is the only positive evidence produced, because it names the layer that rejected each mutant: FRAME_SIZE_ERROR and PROTOCOL_ERROR come from the framing layer, COMPRESSION_ERROR from HPACK.
comparison_axis_note: Cross-stack comparison requires identical --radamsa-seed AND identical H2 server-side limits (max-concurrent-streams, max-frame-size, max-header-list-size). Different limits change what gets rejected at the protocol layer vs the parser layer.
